obligations.note: Retention.isPurgeDue now honours a legal hold only when the case is DECLINED (`isLegalHold() && status() == DECLINED`). A WITHDRAWN case on legal hold becomes purge-due once the retention period passes, which breaks 'never while a legal hold applies'. No exception for RET-1 or mortgage.retention exists in the register.

Ticket CHG-25088 is a standard ticket. Change manager Erik Brandt approved it on 2026-10-22, before the change was opened. Its components (mortgage.retention) cover the only touched file, Retention.java.
Declan Farrell gave a code_review approval. He holds change_approver for baseline-mortgage and is a different person from the author, Tomas Ortega.
The approval names head commit c0b6b8ee, which is the only commit in the change.

run.json claims a run on c0b6b8ee. However, every JUnit report is timestamped 2026-10-23T13:30, a day before that commit was authored (2026-10-24T16:36), and the reports come from a developer machine (dev-laptop-7.local), not ci-runner-03. So the reports cannot show the suite passing on the final commit, including the RET-1 control test sampledPurgeRespectsHold.

summary: The one-line change narrows the legal-hold guard so it applies only to declined cases. Withdrawn applications on legal hold would therefore have their NPI purged, which directly violates RET-1, and no exception covers this. The CI evidence is also invalid: the JUnit reports predate the head commit and were produced on a developer laptop, so CHG-4 is not met. The ticket and the independent approval are in order, but the RET-1 violation alone requires rejection.
